text:
Sam: saw a hosted node OOM at scale during a 5k-long-context batch, attaching quick notes from the profiler :disappointed:
Priya: can you paste the stack or flamegraph?
Sam: flame shows huge KV cache fragmentation + repeated small-page evicts, CPU kernel selection flapping between fast-gemm and fallback path which spikes mem transiently. short paste: `kv_alloc: +45%`, `evict_loop` thrash, `kernel_select()` toggles on sequence >2048
Miguel: is this the same host that got the batch spike earlier?
Sam: yes, same pool. spike correlates with a client sending long chat sessions + many small parallel requests (50 concurrent). batching heuristics tried to batch, but KV reuse was low so prefix copies exploded.
Tanya: TL;DR: long contexts + bad batching = alloc growth + fragmentation -> OOM. we need a graceful degrade path.
Priya: agree. quick mitigations we can ship today: 1) force kvcache compaction on eviction boundary, 2) backoff batching when reuse ratio < 0.2, 3) temporary max_context cap per request for affected pool.
Miguel: for compaction, do we have a cheap op? `kv.compact_async()` exists but currently runs at low priority and doesn't free slabs quickly. straight-line compaction might cause latency blips.
Sam: i sketched a lightweight synchronous compact-on-evict that merges adjacent free slots without full defrag. cheap and local to slab. benchmarked on small sim: 20% less fragmentation, ~5ms tail.
Tanya: can you post that snippet?
Sam: ```
// on eviction path
if (slab.free_runs > COMPACT_THRESHOLD) {
  slab.compact_trim_fast(); // merges short free runs
  slab.record_compact_metric();
}
```
Priya: nice. also add a telemetry gauge for "reuse_ratio" so we can autotune batching. right now heuristics only use batch_latency and qps.
Miguel: kernel selection flapping is interesting — when sequence length jumps past 2048 we pick kernel B (more memory friendly) but falling back to kernel A on next request forces reallocation patterns. need sticky kernel choice per connection/session.
Tanya: yes, sticky kernel by session would reduce churn. short term: pin kernel after first selection for 30s.
Sam: rollout plan proposal: canary patch to 10% of hosted pool: enable compact-on-evict + batching backoff (reuse_ratio threshold) + kernel pin TTL=30s. monitor mem_gauge, evict_rate, tail_latency.
Priya: add alert: if host mem_gauge > 85% trigger per-host request reduction policy (reject long contexts, fallback to short-mode with warning).
eng-bot: deploy started for canary group `hosted-pool-c-1` (build rb-2026.3.428)
Miguel: i've got a small profiler script to run on canary to confirm compaction effect. will run after deploy finishes.
Sam: thanks — if compaction shows >15% drop in live fragmentation and evict churn drops, we can promote. if not, revert and try more aggressive per-request context cap.
Priya: who owns the rollback playbook? Miguel?
Miguel: i'll own rollback. I've added a runbook note: if spillback exceeds 3/min or evict_rate doubles, rollback immediately.
Tanya: I'll update the postmortem template with the kernel-selection notes and add an action to add reuse_ratio telemetry to the runtime.
Sam: ok moving to implement PRs: sam:kv-compact-fast, priya:reuse-telemetry, miguel:kernel-pin-ttl. tagging for visibility @eng-sre @eng-runtime :thumbsup:
Priya: quick Q — do we also want a config knob per-customer to opt out of aggressive compaction? some enterprise customers dislike any extra tail latency.
Tanya: yes expose `kv.compaction_mode: off|lazy|aggressive` default lazy for canary. enterprise can set off.
Sam: deployed canary went healthy, eng-bot reports no new OOMs in group after 10m. will keep monitoring.
eng-bot: deploy succeeded: rb-2026.3.428 canary -> hosted-pool-c-1. metrics: mem_gauge median -4%, evict_rate -32%
Miguel: early sign looks good. schedule a longer 4-hour canary and then we decide promote/rollback.
Priya: noted. updating alerts and dashboards now.
Tanya: thanks everyone — great fast triage. will follow up in the postmortem thread with timelines and customer impact notes. :rocket:
